links.outcome: Zero-shot medical QA accuracy with versus without retrieval augmentation on MedQA USMLE
links.effect: Retrieval augmentation significantly improved zero-shot accuracy; best configuration (dense retrieval with query reformulation and reranking) reached 60.49% accuracy.
links.quote: Results show that retrieval augmentation significantly improves zero-shot medical question answering performance.

unlisted_practices: Comparing embedding models, dense vs. other retrieval strategies, query reformulation, and cross-encoder reranking in RAG pipelines
Using domain-specialized language models to better exploit retrieved medical evidence
Balancing retrieval effectiveness against computational cost and throughput

screen.practice: retrieval grounding (RAG) with query reformulation and reranking
screen.reason: Empirically tests and compares the impact of retrieval grounding (RAG) components (query reformulation, dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking) added to LLMs on a medical benchmark dataset (MedQA).
